trend.title: Trepp: Foreclosures Reach 23% of Resolved CMBS Balance in 2026 as Modifications Fall to 37% and 20% of 2024 Modifications Return to Special Servicing
trend.scope: U.S. CMBS loans resolved from special servicing (Trepp data, as reported by CRE Daily)
trend.metric: Modifications 37% of resolved balance in 2026 (54% in 2024); foreclosures 23%; 20% of loans modified in 2024 back with the special servicer within a year; office 29%; $71.7 billion in special servicing, five times the October 2019 level
trend.summary: CRE Daily, citing Trepp, reports that modifications fell to 37% of resolved CMBS balance in 2026 from 54% in 2024, while foreclosures reached 23%. Of loans modified in 2024, 20% were back with the special servicer within a year, and office fared worst, with 29% of its latest workouts returning. CRE Daily puts the amount in special servicing at $71.7 billion, five times the October 2019 level.
trend.significance: Fewer loans are leaving special servicing through a modification and more through foreclosure, and a modified loan that returns to the special servicer has already used its first workout. Borrowers and guarantors on loans modified in 2024 should expect less forbearance on a second default, and lenders and servicers should prepare for more receiver motions, foreclosure suits and guaranty claims on loans that were already extended once.
